I led the rebuild end to end, reporting to senior HR leadership and partnering with Segal to accelerate the work and align to best practices.

My responsibility was clear: define the compensation philosophy, establish a job architecture, and build a market pricing approach the organization could consistently apply.

The work was not treated as a project with a fixed end date. It was designed as an operating approach that could hold through leadership changes, staffing shifts, and ongoing organizational growth.

Managers could clearly explain pay decisions. Recruiting saw a measurable reduction in offer-stage loss. Compensation moved from a reactive, request-driven function to a governed approach with a defined philosophy, structured job architecture, and consistent market pricing.

The most important outcome was not a metric. Leadership gained a clear and defensible answer to the question: why does this role pay what it pays? That answer held up under scrutiny across the organization.

Leads compensation, HRIS, and payroll for a 6,000-employee Level 1 trauma and academic medical center. Runs the three functions as one integrated operating model — roughly $33M disbursed monthly across three payroll cycles, with a zero-error operating standard. Approaches HR for a 6,000-employee Level 1 academic medical center as an integrated operating model: unified data, governed decisions, quiet execution.

Director of Compensation, HRIS, and Payroll
UT Medical Center  ·  2023 — Present

  • Lead compensation, HRIS, and payroll for a 6,000-employee academic medical center — ~$33M disbursed monthly across three payroll cycles (monthly, biweekly, supplemental).
  • Delivered a full-lifecycle replacement of a legacy UKG Kronos deployment with Infor Workforce Management — RFP through vendor management, hard cutover deadline, no operational disruption.
  • Rebuilt the compensation function from a transactional posture into a governed operating model: documented philosophy, owned job architecture, disciplined market pricing cycle.
  • Own the HR technology ecosystem end to end — HRIS, ATS, LMS, time and attendance, and integrations to Finance and clinical operations.
  • Direct workforce data governance so leadership questions resolve to one answer across HR, Finance, and operations.
  • Operate the three functions as one integrated system, with cross-function alignment built into the design rather than patched after.

• Kronos → Infor WFM cutover delivered on a hard end-of-life deadline with no operational disruption.
  • Compensation function rebuilt from a transactional posture into a governed operating model.
  • Workforce data aligned across HR, Finance, and operations — from inconsistent cross-function answers to one-version truth.
  • Three payroll cycles per month maintained at a zero-error operating standard across ~50 scheduled runs per year.
